simple.meaning: פְּשַׁר (pᵉshar) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to interpret.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Daniel, beginning at Daniel 5:12. The surrounding contexts include kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פְּשַׁר (H6590) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: פְּשַׁר (pᵉshar) / H6590 is traced through Daniel 5:12, Daniel 5:16 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H6590. peshar [ מְּשַׁר ] verb interpret (a dream) ( ᵑ7 id. , Syriac , perhaps Egyptian Aramaic פשר Lzb 355 SAC 100 (Arabic loan-word, see Frä 263 ); Assyrian pašâru ); — Pe`al Infinitive לְמִפְשַׁר Dan 5:16 , accusative of congnate meaning with verb פִשְׁרִין Pa`el Participle active מְפַשַׁר Dan 5:12 , accusative חֶלְמִין .

occurrences.englishText: because an excellent spirit, knowledge, understanding, interpreting of dreams, showing of dark sentences, and dissolving of doubts were found in the same Daniel, whom the king named Belteshazzar. Now let Daniel be called, and he will show the interpretation.”

But I have heard of you, that you can give interpretations, and dissolve doubts. Now if you can read the writing, and make known to me its interpretation, you shall be clothed with purple, and have a chain of gold around your neck, and shall be the third ruler in the kingdom.”
